defects.justification: The SSRF guard resolves the host in isPublicHost() and then lets HttpClient resolve it again for the real request, so a DNS-rebinding host passes the check and the fetch hits 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254; the blocklist also misses ranges such as NAT64 64:ff9b::/96, 0.0.0.0/8 and 198.18/15. Fix by connecting to the vetted address (or via an egress proxy); the README admits the gap but it is still a blocker for a server fetching user URLs.

HttpRequest.timeout only bounds the wait for response headers; the body is then read from an InputStream with no read deadline, so a server that trickles bytes holds the request thread indefinitely. Title fetching is synchronous on an 8-thread fixed pool, so a handful of such links make the whole service unresponsive.

titleFetcherRefusesInternalAddresses asserts null for internal targets, but every one of these fetches would return null anyway (nothing listening / the app's own JSON 404 is not HTML / connect timeout), so the test passes even if isPublicHost() is deleted. It should test isPublicHost() directly or stand up an HTML server on loopback.
